item.title: Model Context Protocol: Why This Matters More Than You Think
item.description:
Every few months, something gets released that looks like infrastructure plumbing but turns out to matter more than the flashy launches. Model Context Protocol (MCP) is one of those things.

If you’re a developer working with LLMs, MCP will change how you integrate AI into your workflows. Here’s an early-adopter perspective on what it is, why it matters, and how to actually use it.

What Problem Does MCP Solve?

Today’s AI tools are context-starved. You paste code into ChatGPT, upload files to Claude, manually copy database schemas into prompts. Every session starts from scratch. Every context window is a blank slate.

item.title: Building a Code Analyzer with Go and tree-sitter
item.description:
Pyscn is a code quality analyzer for Python that I contribute to. It finds dead code, code clones, coupling issues, and complexity hotspots. It’s written in Go, uses tree-sitter for parsing, and processes over 100,000 lines per second.

The interesting engineering decisions are in how it detects dead code through control flow analysis, finds duplicated code across clone types 1-4 with LSH acceleration, and integrates with AI coding assistants via MCP.
